subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should external messaging-channel turns default to a safe final-only/message-tool-only delivery model, or should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text replies as the default and add narrower leak guards?
rationale: The safer behavior reduces security and message-delivery leaks, but current docs and tests preserve automatic visible replies for compatibility, so automation cannot choose the default policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt safe external-channel default
options.body: Make external channel output require explicit message-tool or final-only semantics by default, with migration/doctor/docs coverage and opt-out only where maintainers intentionally preserve legacy behavior.

options.title: Keep automatic default with targeted guards
options.body: Preserve legacy bare-text replies and land narrower filters for commentary, reasoning, NO_REPLY, and cron paths, accepting that some model narration remains harder to classify.

options.title: Split by chat context
options.body: Use message-tool-only for shared rooms and high-risk autonomous/cron paths while keeping DMs automatic until a later migration decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt safe external-channel default
recommendation.body: Make external channel output require explicit message-tool or final-only semantics by default, with migration/doctor/docs coverage and opt-out only where maintainers intentionally preserve legacy behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the central phase-suppression work and are the strongest available routing signal for the compatibility/security decision on current delivery defaults.
